video.summary: Chalkline index.html (6595 lines, v212) carries two generations of export code side by side. (A) In-browser MediaRecorder/canvas paths (exportClip 5851, compileReel 6020, recordClipScreen 5792, exportPNG 5235, snapstill 5259, recordClipDirect 5752) plus a stack of readback probes (probeBlack 1719, videoReadable 1747, videoReadablePlaying 1763, VF/MediaStreamTrackProcessor 5421, black guard 5921-5926) whose sole purpose is to detect that this PC's 4K decode lands on a hardware overlay the browser cannot read. All of those produce black on this machine (except recordClipDirect, which re-encodes to VP9/WebM in real time with no markup). (B) The proven path: build4KBat (5558-5661) plans each clip as an ordered list of pieces (mov footage at rate 1 or a slow-mo rate with timed transparent markup overlays; frz freeze frames held N seconds with the freeze markup on; optional title card), renders every overlay as a full-source-resolution transparent PNG from the vector markup layer (never touching the video), embeds the PNGs base64 in a self-contained Windows .bat, and has ffmpeg cut/overlay/setpts+atempo/concat at 3840x2160 H.264 (libx264 crf 18, yuv420p, aac 192k 48k stereo, -r from ffprobe, timescale 15360). The desktop port should keep only: the mark/shape data model (1250-1260, 2677-2682, 3735, 3806-3826), the vector renderer paint()/paintCaption()/paintTitleCard() (4568-4752, 5069-5091, 5986-6018), the timing helpers freezeStops/shapeAlphaAt/motionWindows/clipPieces/atempoChain (3794-3804, 4275-4293, 5522-5557), and re-implement build4KBat's ffmpeg command sequence as direct process spawns writing PNGs and outputs with real filesystem paths. Everything that reads pixels back from the <video> element must go through ffmpeg instead.

video.data_model:
SESSION S (1250-1260, persisted 6512-6516): pads[] {label,color,pre,post,ask}; padsV; lineWt (0.6-3, default 1, multiplies every stroke in paint()); marks[]; tomb[] (deleted ids); offset (seconds, global shift added to every mark time by clipStart/clipEnd 1792-1793); videoName (filename only — no path exists in the browser); videoKey (name__size); autoEditNew; defaultPlayer; watchMark; vfCap ('ok'|'fail'|'unsupported'); fps (int, default 25, detected 2250-2275). Export settings persisted alongside: exportRes, exportFpsV, titleSecs, h264out (output folder string), clipSort.

CLIP / MARK m (created 2677-2682, 2708-2713, 3319-3324; migrated 3806-3826): id 'm'+Date.now()+4 random chars; t = seconds in the video's own timeline MINUS S.offset (tag time minus #taglag reaction lag when playing); padIndex (-1 for custom); label (title text, uppercased on title cards, sanitised via safe() for filenames); color (COLORS key: ours #3B9EFF, theirs #FF5B44, space/flood #FFC93C, path #B6FF5C, ball #FFFFFF); pre (seconds before, default 2), post (seconds after, default 7) -> export window [clipStart, clipEnd] = [max(0,t+offset-pre), t+offset+post]; ask (coach prompt, not exported); caption (short sentence; painted as the bottom caption bar on EVERY overlay PNG and on the title card); notes (free text in #clipnotes, stored 2037, not exported directly — 'Apply at freeze' turns it into a text shape); shapes[]; player (legacy string) / players[] (array of names; export scope filter and per-player groups); u (last-edit ms); kind ('highlight'|'learning'|absent; compileReel's #reelkind filter and title-card badge); exported (ms timestamp tick); slow[] = [{from,to,rate}] — ABSOLUTE video seconds (vid.currentTime space, offset already applied), rate from RATES <1 (0.1/0.25/0.5, default 0.25), sorted by from, clamped to the clip by clipPieces; freezes[] = [{at, hold}] — ABSOLUTE video seconds, hold 0.5..30 step 0.5 (default freezeHoldDefault=2; notes-created freezes use #hold||3); legacy freezeAt migrated into each shape's t.

SHAPE s (pushed at 3673-3736, 3870, 3877, 2110): tool ∈ {spot, circle, ground, arrow(Run), runpen, pass, lob(Over top), option, line, chain(Connect), curve, zone(Space), wedge(Lane), scan, pen, disc(Marker), text, callout}; color (COLORS key); t = beat time in ABSOLUTE video seconds (beatSnap 3785: current time, or an existing beat within 0.4s) — ground rings take t from kf[0].t; COORDINATES: a, b, c = {x,y} normalised 0..1 of the video FRAME (pt() 3630 divides by the letterboxed draw canvas rect which exactly matches the video rect via fitCanvas 1569-1587; paint() multiplies by W,H) so the same shape renders correctly at 3840x2160; pts[] (pen, runpen, chain; zone stores 3-10 corner pts via planeCorners/addZoneCorner, older zones use a/b bbox); r (ground ring radius as a fraction of width, default 0.05/0.06); kf[] = [{t,x,y}] keyframes for ground rings interpolated by groundCenter(s,time) 4180; spread (scan cone half-width factor, default 0.42); text (disc number / text / callout body, '\n' hard breaks); fs (font px at the 900px-wide reference; actual px = fs*max(1,W/900); default textSize 19; disc uses 15*scale mono); w (optional normalised text-box width -> word wrap); _notes (flag: the notes text box); label (inline label text on arrow/pass/option/lob/curve/line, drawLineLabel 4767); bow (signed curvature; curve default 0.26*(flip?-1:1)); flip; plane (0/1/2… tilt style for 3D-plane arrows, drawPlanedArrow 5021); linger (undefined = default global hold; 0 = freeze-only; >0 = seconds after beat, fades over last 0.5s); keep (1 = stays from beat to clip end); transient: _alpha (set by callers before paint), _live (drag preview).

VISIBILITY RULE shapeAlphaAt(s,t,hold,burnAll) 4275-4292 (t = absolute video time, hold = #hold global, burnAll = #burnmode==='all'): burnAll -> 1; ground with kf and no linger/keep -> t>=kf[0].t-0.1 ? 1:0; s.t==null -> 0; keep -> t>=s.t-0.1 ? 1:0; linger===0 -> 1 only in [s.t-0.1, s.t+0.15] (or during the live hold); else winEnd = s.t+max(linger>0?linger:hold, 0.1), 0 outside [s.t-0.05, winEnd], linear fade to 0 over the last 0.5s when linger>0. Export split of the same rule: freeze pieces use markupPNGb64(m, t) (this rule at t with alpha) 5481-5491; motion pieces use motionWindows 5522-5534 = only keep/linger>0 shapes, window [max(start,t0), keep?end:min(end,t0+linger)], grouped by identical window, rendered at alpha 1 (no fade) by shapesPNGb64 5511.

PROVEN RECIPE = build4KBat(clips, wantReel) at 5558-5661, using clipPieces 5536-5550, motionWindows 5522-5534, atempoChain 5553-5557, freezeStops 3794-3803, markupPNGb64 5481-5491, shapesPNGb64 5511-5517, titleCardPNGb64 5504-5508.

INPUTS (read at call time): name = S.videoName (filename only); outDir = #h264out text trimmed of trailing slashes (empty -> the .bat's own folder); cardSecs = max(1, #titlesecs||5); cards = #titlecards.checked (title cards only when wantReel && cards); holdV = #hold (global freeze hold, default 3); burnAll = #burnmode==='all' (inside markupPNGb64); W,H = vid.videoWidth/videoHeight (3840x2160); S.lineWt; clip list = [curClip] or all clips passing clipInScope sorted by t.

SHARED ENCODER STRING enc (5564): -r %R% -c:v libx264 -crf 18 -preset veryfast -pix_fmt yuv420p -c:a aac -b:a 192k -ar 48000 -ac 2 -video_track_timescale 15360   (%R% = integer fps from ffprobe; identical params on every piece so the final concat can be -c copy).

FPS DETECTION (5635-5638): FP = ffmpeg path with 'ffmpeg' replaced by 'ffprobe'; R = round(num/den) of `ffprobe -v error -select_streams v:0 -show_entries stream=r_frame_rate -of csv=p=0 "<SRC>"` (parsed by PowerShell: split on '/', [math]::Round(a/b)); default 30 if unreadable.

WORK DIR + OUTPUT (5620-5624, 5647): OUTDIR = outDir (mkdir if missing); W = "%OUTDIR%\\.chalkline-work" (rd /s /q then mkdir — deliberately on the output drive because C: is nearly full); all intermediates go in W; W is deleted at the end (5647). Source discovery (5616-5619): SRC = %1 if dragged onto the .bat, else first existing of <batDir>\\<name>, <outDir>\\<name>, %USERPROFILE%\\Dropbox\\KIDS SPORTS VIDEOS\\<name>, E:\\Chalkline\\<name>, E:\\<name>. ffmpeg discovery (5625-5634): where ffmpeg -> %LOCALAPPDATA%\\Microsoft\\WinGet\\Links\\ffmpeg.exe -> winget install --id Gyan.FFmpeg -e. PNG transport (5642, 5654): every PNG is appended after 'exit /b' as lines '#PNG:<file>#', <base64>, '#END#'; a PowerShell one-liner reads the .bat, concatenates each block, [Convert]::FromBase64String -> [IO.File]::WriteAllBytes(W\\<file>). PNGs are deduplicated by key via addPNG (5567): 'card'+id, 'frz'+id+'@'+t, 'win'+id+'@'+from+'-'+to, 'cap'+id -> p1.png, p2.png…

PLAN PER CLIP (clipPieces 5536-5549): start = clipStart(m) = max(0, m.t+S.offset-m.pre); end = clipEnd(m) = m.t+S.offset+m.post. freezes = freezeStops(m,start,end,holdV) [shape beats @holdV ∪ m.freezes @own hold, merged within 0.15s keeping the longer hold, restricted to (start+0.1, end-0.1)] then filter hold>0. zones = m.slow.map({from:max(start,from), to:min(end,to), rate:rate||0.25}).filter(len>0.05 && 0<rate<1). cut points = {start, end} ∪ {freeze t} ∪ {zone from, to}, sorted. For consecutive (a,b): if b-a>0.05 push {type:'mov', a, b, rate: (zone containing (a+b)/2)?.rate ?? 1}; then if a freeze has t==b (within 1e-6) push {type:'frz', t, hold}. windows = motionWindows(m,start,end): for each shape with keep or linger>0: t0 = s.t ?? m.t; from = max(start,t0); to = keep ? end : min(end, t0+linger); skip if to-from<0.05; group shapes by identical (from.toFixed(2)|to.toFixed(2)).

COMMANDS EMITTED PER CLIP ci (5568-5604), output out = safe(label)+'-'+round(m.t)+'s-4K.mp4':
1) Title card (only wantReel && cards) 5572-5576: PNG = paintTitleCard at W×H (opaque). 
   ffmpeg -y -loop 1 -i "W\\pN.png" -f lavfi -i anullsrc=r=48000:cl=stereo -filter_complex "[0]format=yuv420p[v]" -map "[v]" -map 1:a -t <cardSecs> <enc> "W\\c{ci}_card.mp4"
   -> appended to reelParts only (not to the clip's own file).
2) For each piece k (z = c{ci}_p{k}.mp4):
   FRZ (5579-5583): PNG = markupPNGb64(m, t) — transparent W×H, shapes with shapeVisibleAt(s,t,holdV,burnAll) drawn with their shapeAlphaAt alpha, plus caption bar. Frame grab: 
     ffmpeg -y -ss <t.toFixed(3)> -i "SRC" -frames:v 1 "W\\c{ci}_f{k}.png"
   Hold: 
     ffmpeg -y -loop 1 -i "W\\c{ci}_f{k}.png" -i "W\\pN.png" -f lavfi -i anullsrc=r=48000:cl=stereo -filter_complex "[0][1]overlay=0:0,format=yuv420p[v]" -map "[v]" -map 2:a -t <hold.toFixed(2)> <enc> "W\\c{ci}_p{k}.mp4"
   MOV (5584-5597): overlays ovs = for each window w intersecting [p.a,p.b] with length>0.05: {file: shapesPNGb64(m, w.shapes) [alpha 1 + caption], a:max(w.from,p.a), b:min(w.to,p.b)}; if m.caption and no windows: one caption-only PNG (shapesPNGb64(m,[])) spanning the whole piece. Filter graph (times are relative to piece start and divided by rate because setpts runs first):
     vf = "[0:v]setpts=(PTS-STARTPTS)/<rate>[v0]" then for each overlay i: ";[v{i}][{i+1}:v]overlay=0:0:enable='between(t,<((oa-a)/rate).toFixed(3)>,<((ob-a)/rate).toFixed(3)>)'[v{i+1}]" then ";[vLast]format=yuv420p[v]"
     af = rate===1 ? "[0:a]asetpts=PTS-STARTPTS[a]" : "[0:a]asetpts=PTS-STARTPTS,<atempoChain(rate)>[a]"  where atempoChain: while rem<0.5 push 'atempo=0.5', rem*=2; then push 'atempo='+rem.toFixed(3) if rem≠1 (0.5 -> atempo=0.5; 0.25 -> atempo=0.5,atempo=0.5; 0.1 -> atempo=0.5,atempo=0.5,atempo=0.5,atempo=0.8).
     ffmpeg -y -ss <a.toFixed(3)> -to <b.toFixed(3)> -i "SRC" [-i "W\\pX.png" …] -filter_complex "<vf>;<af>" -map "[v]" -map "[a]" <enc> "W\\c{ci}_p{k}.mp4"
     (Both -ss and -to are INPUT options before -i; with ffmpeg 8.1 -to is an absolute input position, proven working. A port may equivalently use -ss a -t (b-a). Note the source is yuvj420p full-range; format=yuv420p + libx264 handled it fine in the proven runs.)
   Every piece z is pushed to both parts (this clip) and reelParts (reel).
3) Concat this clip (5601-5602): write list{ci}.txt with lines "file 'c{ci}_p{k}.mp4'" (relative names; ffmpeg resolves relative to the list file's dir), then
     ffmpeg -y -f concat -safe 0 -i "W\\list{ci}.txt" -c copy "OUTDIR\\<out>"
4) Reel (5605-5611, when wantReel): reel.txt = all reelParts in order (card0, c0 pieces…, card1, c1 pieces…) then
     ffmpeg -y -f concat -safe 0 -i "W\\reel.txt" -c copy "OUTDIR\\chalkline-reel-4K-<YYYY-MM-DD>.mp4"
5) Tail: rd /s /q W; list outputs; 'send as a Document on WhatsApp'; pause. In the app: every exported clip gets c.exported=Date.now(); save; renderClips (5658).

WHY IT WORKS: no video pixels are ever read in the browser — only the vector markup layer is rasterised (transparent canvas, no drawImage(video)), so the PNGs are always correct; ffmpeg does 100% of decode/composite/encode at 3840x2160.

PORTING NOTES: (1) Replace the .bat with an in-app job runner: write p*.png from canvas.toBlob(), run the exact command list sequentially with spawn, parse stderr progress, delete the work dir. (2) Keep work dir on the output drive (E:) — C: has 4.8 GB free. (3) Keep enc identical across pieces so the -c copy concat stays valid; -video_track_timescale 15360 and -r R avoid timebase mismatches; anullsrc gives cards/freezes an audio stream so concat streams line up. (4) fps from ffprobe (r_frame_rate), not from the browser. (5) Freeze frame grab at the exact t (input-side -ss with -frames:v 1 gives the nearest decoded frame at/after t). (6) The v1 generator (5673-5747) differs: %TEMP% work dir, output beside the .bat, browser fps, no slow-mo/windows/cards, overlays the whole-clip markup PNG in one pass when there are no freezes (`[0][1]overlay=0:0,format=yuv420p` with `-map 0:a?`) — do not port. (7) Clean-cut variants (5407, 6169): "-ss S -i src -t D -c:v libx264 -crf 18 -preset veryfast -pix_fmt yuv420p -c:a aac -b:a 192k" — subsumed by a mov-only plan; a stream-copy cut (-c copy) would be faster if frame accuracy at keyframes is acceptable, but the proven exports re-encode.

ui.summary: index.html (6595 lines, v212) is a single-page app: 13 lines of head/meta, ~555 lines of CSS (lines 15-570), ~615 lines of HTML (572-1184: header, one Studio section with four columns [Clips | Stage | Markup | Clip/Export], a Help section, a toast and five <dialog>s), and ~5400 lines of vanilla JS (1186-6595) with zero library dependencies. State is one mutable global object `S` (pads, marks[], tomb[], offset, videoName/videoKey, defaultPlayer, watchMark, lineWt, autoEditNew, vfCap) plus a few dozen module-level `let`s for transient UI state (curClip, selection, tool, colour, zoom, loupe, immersive, undo stack, drag structs). Persistence is a debounced JSON blob in localStorage key `chalkline:session` (350 ms after any change), a per-video library (`chalkline:vid:<name>__<size>`, 20 most recent) so switching matches restores their clips, a separate `chalkline:thumbs` store, `chalkline:sync`, and IndexedDB `chalkline/kv` holding File System Access handles (`videoHandle`, `exportDir`). Clip geometry: mark.t is the tag moment in video seconds MINUS the global offset; clipStart = t+offset-pre, clipEnd = t+offset+post; every shape/freeze/slow-section time is ABSOLUTE video seconds; all shape coordinates are normalised 0..1 of the video frame and stroke/font sizes scale with max(1, W/900). Rendering is one `paint(ctx,W,H,shapes,extra)` function that is reused for the live canvas, thumbnails, PNG stills and the transparent overlay PNGs embedded in the ffmpeg .bat. GLOBAL SESSION `S` (index.html 1250-1260, persisted by save() 6508-6516):
- pads: Pad[] where Pad = {label:string, color:'ours'|'theirs'|'space'|'path'|'ball'|'flood', pre:number (seconds before), post:number (seconds after), ask:string}. Default 7 pads (1239-1247).
- padsV: number — pads migration version (0→1 adds 'Attacking', 1→2 forces pre 2 / post 7). Currently 2.
- lineWt: number 0.6..3 (global stroke multiplier, step 0.2; default 1).
- marks: Mark[] — the clips (see below).
- tomb: string[] — ids of deleted marks (for sync merge).
- offset: number seconds — global shift applied to every mark when computing on-screen time.
- videoName: string — file name of the loaded match. videoKey: string — `${name with [^\w.-] → _}__${size bytes}` (1425), used as the per-video library slot key.
- autoEditNew: boolean (+ aeV:1 written on save as a 'default changed' marker).
- defaultPlayer: string — applied as `player` to new clips.
- watchMark: number|null — Spot bookmark in ABSOLUTE video seconds.
- vfCap: 'ok'|'fail'|'unsupported'|undefined — VideoFrame-capture probe verdict (5441).
- Also written into the same blob but not on S: exportRes ('480'|'720'|'1080'|'source'), exportFpsV ('24'..'60'), titleSecs (string), h264out (output folder path string, default 'C:\\Users\\ChadFerguson\\Dropbox\\KIDS SPORTS VIDEOS' in HTML), clipSort ('time'|'player'|'category'|'kind'), fps (number, frame-step rate, default 25).

MARK / CLIP object (created in tagNow 2677-2682, customTag 2708-2713, autoClipForFreeze 3319-3324; normalised by migrateMark 3806-3826):
- id: string — 'm' + Date.now() + 4 base36 chars.
- t: number — tag moment in video seconds MINUS S.offset (tagNow: at = max(0, currentTime − lag) − offset). Real video time of the moment = t + S.offset. This is the ONLY offset-relative time in the model.
- padIndex: number — index into S.pads, −1 for custom tags.
- label: string; color: colour key (see pads); ask: string (coaching question); caption: string (burned into exports as bottom bar, word-count target 15).
- notes: string — raw text of #clipnotes (not rendered; the rendered form is a shape with _notes).
- pre: number seconds; post: number seconds. clipStart = max(0, t+offset−pre) (1792); clipEnd = t+offset+post (1793). Trims snap to 0.5 s.
- shapes: Shape[] (see below).
- player: string (legacy single) OR players: string[] (current; setClipPlayers deletes `player`). playersOf() reads either.
- u: number — ms epoch of last edit (touch()).
- kind?: 'highlight'|'learning' (absent = neither).
- exported?: number — ms epoch when any export was produced for it (drives ✓ flag).
- freezes?: {at:number (ABSOLUTE video seconds, snapped 0.1 s, clamped to clip window), hold:number seconds 0.5..30 step 0.5}[] sorted by at; property deleted when empty.
- slow?: {from:number, to:number (ABSOLUTE seconds, snapped 0.1 s, to−from ≥ 0.1), rate:number (0.1|0.25|0.5)}[] sorted by from; deleted when empty. Legacy single object migrated to array.
- Legacy: freezeAt (removed by migrateMark: each shape lacking t gets freezeAt or t).

SHAPE / MARKUP object (curClip.shapes[]; all coordinates NORMALISED 0..1 of the video frame, x right, y down; times ABSOLUTE video seconds):
- tool: 'spot'|'circle'|'ground'|'arrow'|'runpen'|'pass'|'lob'|'option'|'line'|'chain'|'curve'|'zone'|'wedge'|'scan'|'pen'|'disc'|'text'|'callout'.
- color: colour key (COLORS 1230-1237; 'flood' is an alias of 'space' #FFC93C).
- a?: {x,y} — anchor/start (spot centre, circle corner, arrow tail, text top-left, callout text end, disc centre, wedge apex, scan eyes).
- b?: {x,y} — end/target (spot radius point, circle opposite corner, arrow tip, callout arrowhead, scan reach). c?: {x,y} — third point (wedge second base corner).
- pts?: {x,y}[] — polyline for pen/runpen/chain, or ≥3 polygon corners for zone (older zones used a/b and derive 4 corners via zonePts 4813).
- t: number — beat time (absolute video seconds) the mark belongs to; set by beatSnap (3785). Ground rings: t = kf[0].t.
- linger?: number — 0 = freeze-only, N>0 = show N seconds after t then 0.5 s fade; undefined = global #hold. keep?: 1 — stay on to clip end (mutually exclusive with linger).
- text?: string (text, callout, disc number). fs?: number — font px at the 900-px reference width (10..60, default textSize 19; line labels default 16). w?: number — normalised text-box width once resized (wraps).
- label?: string — text drawn along a line/arrow (LABEL_TOOLS: arrow, pass, option, lob, curve, line).
- flip?: boolean (curve/lob mirror). bow?: number −3..3 signed curvature (curve/arrow; overrides flip when set). plane?: 1 (3D tapered rendering for arrow/pass/option/lob/curve).
- r?: number — ground ring radius as fraction of frame WIDTH (≥0.01; ellipse ry = 0.42·rx). kf?: {t,x,y}[] — ground ring follow keyframes (sorted, ~0.1 s apart when auto-tracked).
- spread?: number — scan cone half-width ratio of beam length (0.06..2, default 0.42).
- _notes?: true — created by Apply-at-freeze/whole-clip (persisted, used to find/update the box).
- _alpha: number — TRANSIENT render opacity written by shapeAlphaAt but not deleted, so it leaks into saved JSON/sync payloads. _live: {x,y} — transient ground-ring drag preview (deleted on pointerup).
Rendering scale: `scale = max(1, W/900)`; base line width 3.2·scale·lineWt; disc radius 13·scale; head reach 15·scale·lineWt.

THUMBNAILS: Thumbs.map = {[mark.id]: 'data:image/jpeg;base64,…'} (160 × round(160·h/w) px, quality 0.6) in localStorage 'chalkline:thumbs' (1856-1873).

ui.export_pipeline:
ENTRY POINTS (Clip column 902-1006, wired 5136-5141, 5235, 5259, 5302, 6144-6155, 6157, 6195):
1. #export4k → make4KClipBat(curClip) → build4KBat([m], false); #export4kall → make4KAllBat() → build4KBat(filtered marks sorted by t, true). THIS IS THE PROVEN PATH.
2. #exportclip → exportClip(): if S.vfCap==='fail' it toasts and redirects to make4KClipBat (5865); if vfCap!=='ok' and videoReadablePlaying() is false → recordClipScreen (getDisplayMedia); otherwise canvas+MediaRecorder with VF.start(); a 12-frame black guard throws 'black export', sets S.vfCap='fail' and falls back to make4KClipBat (5966-5971).
3. #reelbtn → compileReel(): real-time MediaRecorder of every in-scope clip with title cards (paintTitleCard) and freeze holds; refuses via warnBlank when frames read black.
4. #exportpng → canvas drawImage(vid)+paint+paintCaption (black on this PC); #snapstill → getDisplayMedia crop (black on this PC).
5. Advanced: #exportdirect → recordClipDirect (captureStream, no markup — the one browser recording that worked, but no markups, WebM/MP4 whatever MediaRecorder supports); #exportffcut → ffmpegCutClip (clean cut .bat, crf 18); #exportall → make-all-clips[-player].bat (cuts + concat reel) AND chalkline-session-<date>.json; #exportbatch → per-player text cut lists (1280-wide, crf 23) via writeOut; #makeh264 → h264ConverterBat (1080p/720p/source, optional 60 s test) for making browser-readable copies.
6. #vfprobe/#vfstatus → VF.probe(); VF.autoProbe runs 1.2 s after first play if S.vfCap unset.

THE 4K .BAT ENGINE v2 (build4KBat 5558-5661), per clip m:
- clipPieces(m) (5536): start/end from clipStart/clipEnd; freezes = freezeStops(m,start,end,#hold) with hold>0 (i.e. markup beats at the global hold + manual m.freezes); zones = m.slow clamped to the clip with 0<rate<1; cut points = {start,end} ∪ freeze times ∪ zone edges; walk sorted points producing {type:'mov',a,b,rate} for each gap (rate = zone containing the midpoint, else 1) and {type:'frz',t,hold} after any point that is a freeze. Also windows = motionWindows(m,start,end) (5522): for each shape with keep or linger>0, window [max(start,t0), keep? end : min(end,t0+linger)], grouped by identical window.
- PNG rendering, all at vid.videoWidth×vid.videoHeight (3840×2160) on a transparent canvas using the same paint(): frz → markupPNGb64(m,t) (shapes visible at t per burn mode + hold, with per-shape alpha, plus paintCaption); mov overlays → shapesPNGb64(m, window.shapes) at alpha 1 + caption (or a caption-only PNG when no windows intersect and m.caption exists); reel title cards → titleCardPNGb64 (paintTitleCard: #0C1711 bg, tag-colour bar, 'NN / TT  mm:ss' mono, label in 44px Barlow Condensed, kind badge, caption in #FFC93C). PNGs are de-duplicated by key (addPNG) and embedded as '#PNG:pN.png#' … base64 … '#END#' blocks appended after the batch commands.
- ffmpeg commands (enc = '-r %R% -c:v libx264 -crf 18 -preset veryfast -pix_fmt yuv420p -c:a aac -b:a 192k -ar 48000 -ac 2 -video_track_timescale 15360'):
  card: -loop 1 -i card.png -f lavfi -i anullsrc … -t cardSecs
  frz: extract one frame (-ss t -i SRC -frames:v 1 fr.png), then -loop 1 -i fr.png -i markup.png + anullsrc, overlay=0:0, -t hold
  mov: -ss a -to b -i SRC [-i overlay.png …] -filter_complex '[0:v]setpts=(PTS-STARTPTS)/rate[v0]; [v0][1:v]overlay=0:0:enable=between(t,f1,f2)[v1]…;format=yuv420p[v]; [0:a]asetpts=PTS-STARTPTS[,atempo chain][a]'
  then per-clip concat (-f concat -safe 0 -c copy) → '%OUTDIR%\\<label>-<t>s-4K.mp4'; optional reel concat of all parts → chalkline-reel-4K-<date>.mp4.
- .bat header: finds SRC by name (%~1 drag-drop, script dir, #h264out folder, %USERPROFILE%\\Dropbox\\KIDS SPORTS VIDEOS, E:\\Chalkline, E:), sets OUTDIR (#h264out or script dir), work dir OUTDIR\\.chalkline-work (deliberately on the output drive because C: is full), locates/installs ffmpeg via winget (Gyan.FFmpeg), derives ffprobe path, reads r_frame_rate with PowerShell → %R%, unpacks the base64 PNG blocks with PowerShell, runs the commands, deletes the work dir, marks clips exported (c.exported=Date.now()).
- atempoChain(rate): halves until ≥0.5 then remainder (0.25 → atempo=0.5,atempo=0.5; 0.1 → 0.5,0.5,0.5,0.8).

WHAT A DESKTOP PORT NEEDS TO KEEP: freezeStops/clipPieces/motionWindows planning, paint() as the overlay renderer (transparent PNG at source resolution — it never touches the video, so it is unaffected by the GPU overlay problem), paintCaption/paintTitleCard, atempoChain, the exact ffmpeg filter graphs and encoder flags above, the output naming (safe(label)-<round(t)>s-4K.mp4, chalkline-reel-4K-<date>.mp4), the 'exported' stamp. What it should replace: writing a .bat + PowerShell unpack → spawn ffmpeg/ffprobe directly from Node with PNGs written to a work folder on E:, progress parsed from stderr, then delete work files. Everything under 'Export in the browser', 'Reel (in browser)', 'Export audio' (AudioMix), VF, recordClipDirect/Screen, snapstill, exportpng-via-drawImage, and the h264 converter become unnecessary (stills can be ffmpeg frame + overlay).
ui.update_mechanism: Today: (1) Hosted — GitHub Pages serves the repo root (github.com/Doorstopper/Chalkline, ~208 commits). sw.js (CACHE='chalkline-v212') is network-first for the document (fetch cache:'no-store', falls back to cache offline) and cache-first-with-refresh for icons/manifest/fonts; it does skipWaiting + clients.claim, deletes old caches on activate, and never caches '/chalkline-sync/' or JSON. index.html registers it only when location.protocol starts with http (6521), calls reg.update() on load, every 15 min, on visibilitychange and focus, and reloads once on controllerchange. APP_VERSION='v212' (1219) is shown in #appver; clicking it forces reg.update() + location.reload(). CLAUDE.md 'deploy' routine = bump sw.js CACHE and APP_VERSION → commit → push. (2) Local — 'Create Chalkline shortcut.cmd' writes a Desktop Chalkline.url (InternetShortcut) pointing at file:///<repo>/index.html with chalkline.ico; the SW is skipped on file:// so the local copy is whatever git pull left in the repo. There is no build step, no package.json, no bundler, no tests; every change is a direct edit to index.html by Claude Code.
